6. Now the only dispute to be adjudicated by the Court is qua the claim of plaintiff no. 1 against defendant no.1 for Rs. 1864932/- alongwith pendentelite and future interest qua the first consignment.

7. The claim of plaintiff no. 1:
Towards the services provided for first consignment by the plaintiff no. 1 to the defendant no. 1, a sum of Rs. 54,73,432/- became payable by the defendant no. 1 to the plaintiff no. 1 as per invoices.

However, defendant no. 1 paid only sum of Rs.
36,08,500/- towards the above said amount and hence a sum of Rs. 18,64,932 became due, outstanding, payable by the Defendant No. 1 to Plaintiff.

The services qua second consignment were provided by plaintiff no. 2 to the defendant no. 1 only because defendant no. 1 pressurized the plaintiff to clear the outstanding qua first consignment on the condition that the services of second consignment are provided at discounted rate.

The defendant no. 1 made advance payment of Rs. 08 lacs towards second consignment with assurance to pay the remaining amount qua the first consignment and remaining amount of estimate calculation qua second consignment within 3-4 days.
The Plaintiffs carried the second consignment in seven trucks and all reached Ajmer on March 1, 2018.
However, despite elapse of stipulated time period of 3-4 days, defendant no. 1 failed to make the payment and also started avoiding the Plaintiffs.
The Plaintiffs stopped the trucks at Ajmer.

Thereafter, Plaintiff No. 1 got a legal notice issued to the Defendant M/S BOMBAY RAIPUR LOGISTICS Vs. M/S ARIHANT CARGO CARRIERS PVT LTD M/S ARIHANT CARGO CARRIERS PVT LTD Vs. M/S BOMBAY RAIPUR LOGISTICS Dated 10.07.2025 PRABH by PRABH DEEP KAUR DEEP 2025.07.10

sentences.text: This Court has no territorial jurisdiction to entertain and try the present suit as no part of cause of action as averred by the Plaintiff(s) has arisen within the jurisdiction of this Court.
Defendant No. 1 Company is not having any office within the jurisdiction of this Court.

In fact, the cause of action (if any) has arisen at (a) Kolkata (where the Defendant No.1 is having its registered office), or (b) Anjar Gujarat (from where the Plaintiff No. 2 had loaded the consignment and the Defendant No. 1 had registered the above mentioned FIR, or (c) Ajmer, Rajasthan (from where the trailers were seized by the police officials as case property in above mentioned FIR, or (d) Sh Sagar, Assam (where the Plaintiff No. 2 had to deliver the consignment, (e) Khambat,
Gujarat (from where the Plaintiff No. 1 had loaded consignment) or (f) Panisagar,
Tripura (where the Plaintiff No. 1 had delivered the consignment) or (g) Surajkund,
Faridabad, Haryana (where the payments made by the Defendant No. 1 Company to the Plaintiff were realized).

Thus, the suit is liable to returned to the Plaintiff u/o 7 Rule M/S BOMBAY RAIPUR LOGISTICS Vs. M/S ARIHANT CARGO CARRIERS PVT LTD M/S ARIHANT CARGO CARRIERS PVT LTD Vs. M/S BOMBAY RAIPUR LOGISTICS Dated 10.07.2025 PRABH Digitally by PRABH DEEP KAUR signed DEEP Date:

21. In the delivery of cargo by road transport, specifically by trucks, the general presumption is that time is not essence of the contract and reasonable delay is expected and has to be condoned.
Therefore, delay of 2 weeks cannot be considered as an unexpected or extraorbitant delay in itself.
22. Now defendant no. 1 has claimed that cargo was delivered late, therefore, it is entitled for LD charges.
As per them, the charges have been levied as per industry practice as per standard charges.
However, merely because parties have agreed for late delivery charges, it does not mean that defendant is entitled for the same ipso facto and defendant no. 1 is to prove some damage or injury to claim the LD charges.
Defendant no. 1 has not led any evidence to prove what injury or damages have been caused to the defendant no. 1 due to late delivery of cargo by the plaintiff no. 1 nor defendant no. 1 has pleaded the same anywhere during the pleadings.
Further, defendant no. 1 has not examined any witness anywhere else from the same industry to prove that as per standard practice in the same industry, the delay of two weeks can attract late delivery charges.
Thus, defendant no. 1 has failed to prove that time was essence of the delivery thereby attracting LD charges against plaintiff.

12
In view thereof, merely because cargo was delivered with delay of two weeks, that does not, ipso facto entitle the defendant no. 1 to claim LD charges.
Therefore, defendant no. 1 is not entitled for any LD charges.
Thus, both DWs admitted that the major portion of contract has been executed between parties over the telephonic communication.
Therefore, when the plaintiff had dealt with the defendant over telephonic call while sitting at his office which is within jurisdiction of this Court, the part of cause of action has arisen within jurisdiction of this Court also.
